algorithmFindings.detail: For a report launch, publish the findings as a PDF carousel, with one comparison per page. Multi-image posts averaged 338 impressions versus 1,451 for carousels. Use a single chart or photograph when one image can carry the argument.

publishingBenchmarks.title: Choose the format for the intended response
publishingBenchmarks.finding: Metricool’s personal-profile table reports mean impressions of 1,451.19 for carousels, 1,186.74 for single images and 605.57 for video. Single images lead on mean comments: 2.80 versus 2.38 for carousels. These are observational format averages for January–February 2026; the wider study covers 673,658 posts from 63,108 accounts across two years. Zero-impression and zero-interaction posts are excluded, and outliers retained.
publishingBenchmarks.implication: Test document carousels for multi-step explanations and single-chart posts for discussion. This benchmark does not establish a causal format advantage or supersede Riad’s own video results.

publishingBenchmarks.title: Use the existing volume more consistently
publishingBenchmarks.finding: Buffer’s underlying analysis compares each account with itself using account fixed effects. Engagement-rate differences versus one-post weeks are +0.23, +0.76 and +1.40 percentage points for 2–5, 6–10 and 11+ posts. The sample excludes posts with five or fewer engagements and weeks with no posts; time-varying content and audience factors remain possible confounders. Its reach model estimates lower reach per post at higher frequencies, unlike the broader claim in Buffer’s marketing article.
publishingBenchmarks.implication: Riad published 142 originals across 37 complete Monday–Sunday weeks from 5 January through 20 September 2026: 3.84 per week, a median of 3, with 3 empty weeks and a range of 0–12. A planning target of 3–4 originals per week is a proposed consistency test, not an estimated optimum.

publishingBenchmarks.title: Test afternoon slots in the priority audience’s time zone
publishingBenchmarks.finding: Buffer’s September 2026 analysis of 4.8 million posts identifies Wednesday at 16:00 and Friday at 15:00 and 16:00 as its highest-engagement slots. The publication normalizes results to local time. These are aggregated benchmarks, not results for Riad’s international audience.
publishingBenchmarks.implication: Try Wednesday 16:00 and Friday 15:00 in the priority audience’s local time against current slots, using comparable topics and formats and the same observation window. Choose the audience before converting times for scheduling.

history.title: Professional conversations and network relevance
history.finding: LinkedIn described a two-stage system: retrieve candidate posts, then rank them for each viewer. Its objectives included viewing, conversation and feedback to creators. Network content dominated the system described at that time.
history.implication: Relevant professional relationships were already central. The later changes add ways to recognize useful content; they do not make the network irrelevant.

history.title: Reading becomes a signal, even without a reaction
history.finding: LinkedIn introduced a model predicting whether a reader would skip a post after a short dwell. A higher predicted skip probability reduced the post’s ranking score. The company reported rolling the model out to all members.
history.implication: Reaction counts miss readers who consume a post without responding. A useful opening matters, but this is not evidence for padding captions to increase reading time.

history.title: Knowledge, perspective and substantive replies
history.finding: In a first-hand interview, LinkedIn’s editorial and product leaders described greater emphasis on posts from followed accounts and useful expertise beyond the network. They highlighted a distinct audience, the author’s subject knowledge and meaningful comments.
history.implication: A clear professional position and replies that develop it fit the stated direction. This interview explains product intent, rather than publishing a ranking formula.

history.title: Attention is judged against comparable content
history.finding: LinkedIn described positive long-dwell predictions normalized by attributes including content type, creator type and distribution method. Thresholds adapt from observed behavior. A single duration threshold had favored formats that naturally take longer to consume.
history.implication: Longer captions or videos do not automatically win. The relevant question is whether a piece holds attention relative to comparable content.

history.title: Topic meaning and changing professional interests
history.finding: LinkedIn announced LLM-based retrieval and sequential ranking that connect post meaning with professional profiles and engagement history. The accompanying product update described efforts to reduce recycled low-substance content, engagement bait, automated comments and engagement pods.
history.implication: Develop specific, original explanations for the people making the relevant decision. Treat meaningful exchanges as the objective; do not organize empty comments to manufacture activity.

history.title: LinkedIn reports 40% fewer views of content classified as low quality
history.finding: Chief Product Officer Hari Srinivasan reported 40% fewer views of content LinkedIn classifies as “AI slop” compared with a few weeks earlier. Members had used the new feedback option more than one million times in two weeks. His update described several distribution signals and safeguards against individual reports determining a post’s distribution.
history.implication: This is a company-reported platform trend, not a controlled experiment or a measured penalty for all AI-assisted writing. The update does not publish the classification method or a creator-level reach forecast.

history.title: Sequential ranking lifts engagement by 3.52% in controlled tests
history.finding: LinkedIn’s Feed SR paper reports controlled online tests against the previous production model: 3.52% more likes, comments and reshares, and 2.10% more time spent. The model uses sequences of member interactions. Engagement rose 4.07% among daily users, 3.40% among weekly users and 1.86% among monthly users; the result for new members was not statistically significant. These are relative changes. Version 3 of the paper reports deployment across most Feed traffic.
history.implication: The results measure the ranking system as a whole. They do not isolate the effect of a particular post format, caption length or writing technique.

history.title: A clearer route to relevant people outside the network
history.finding: The Profile Relevance system matches post text, titles and transcripts with members’ professional context. LinkedIn also describes a requirement for this particular recommendation source: a post must first receive a like, comment or share from an unconnected member. In online experiments, the Geo + Engagement variant reduced the overall hide rate by 18.8%; among members with limited activity history, viral engagement increased by 17.7%. These are relative platform-level changes, not percentage-point differences or predictions for a particular creator.
history.implication: Content needs both professional relevance and a real audience response. This is one retrieval source, not a universal rule that one outside comment guarantees distribution.

principles.title: Write for an identifiable professional decision
principles.text: The report’s implication is to name the problem, the affected audience and the evidence needed to act. A post on financing grid connections can be more useful to an investor or energy ministry than a general statement that grids matter. This is an editorial inference from LinkedIn’s relevance systems, not a guaranteed reach tactic.

principles.title: Choose the format that explains the point
principles.text: The reviewed sources do not establish a fixed organic bonus for carousels, videos or long captions. LinkedIn’s 2024 work explicitly addresses bias from formats with naturally longer viewing times. Use a document post to separate evidence into readable steps and video when a direct explanation adds value.

principles.title: Invite expertise, with a reason for the invitation
principles.text: A relevant mention can invite someone into a discussion. The useful outcome is a professional adding evidence, questioning a claim or bringing in a colleague who can use it. Broad requests to tag people, coordinated commenting and automated responses are not the strategy.

principles.title: Treat platform changes as context for the archive
principles.text: This archive records public reactions and comments, not impressions, dwell time, audience composition or donor conversions. Its time trends cannot identify the causal effect of an algorithm update. The six recommendations rest on the reviewed posts and supporting research; platform evidence informs how to test them.

channels.title: Instagram: original material, adapted for viewing
channels.text: Meta describes different ranking systems across surfaces, using several predictions including likely sharing. Its 2024 changes give eligible original content an initial audience and expand distribution for stronger responses. Trial Reels offer a way to test material with non-followers. This supports testing original short explanations, field footage and clean photographs; it does not establish that photographs or designed graphics should disappear.
channels.application: Test clips with a clear opening, subtitles and one idea. Keep a photograph or figure legible at phone size. Compare non-follower reach, viewing retention, shares per reach and relevant profile actions within the same format. Use Trial Reels where available.

channels.title: UNDP website: a lasting source of evidence and expertise
channels.text: Google says its existing search requirements also apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode: accessible, indexable pages with useful text, internal links and appropriate supporting media. No special AI file or schema guarantees inclusion. This supports publishing substantive pages on UNDP’s methods, tools and results, with clear authorship, dated evidence and a contact route.
channels.application: Put essential explanations in the page itself, with a descriptive title and links to methods and data. A PDF can support the page. Measure actual visibility and enquiries; the archive does not establish how often UNDP currently appears in AI answers.

channels.title: Search and AI visibility can now be measured more directly
channels.text: Google announced dedicated generative-AI impression reports in June 2026 and reported a worldwide rollout by 31 August. Microsoft’s October 2026 Topics Portfolio groups a site’s AI grounding queries and citations by topic, where sufficient data exists. These are measures of visibility, not proof of visits or resource mobilization.
channels.application: Ask the website team for the relevant Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools reports. Connect them with tagged campaign links, website enquiries and recorded follow-ups. Keep Google impressions, Bing citations, visits and qualified conversations as separate measures.

assessment.reason: A compact history explains the shift toward attention and professional relevance. Keep the full research separate so the main report reaches Riad’s evidence quickly.

assessment.suggestion: Use more Instagram clips and Reels
assessment.reason: Film short explanations and field observations rather than exporting the same LinkedIn graphic. Select winning formats using Instagram results; this dataset contains no Instagram performance.

assessment.suggestion: Use photographs with less text and design
assessment.reason: Give each visual one job. Keep subtitles on video, enough context in the caption and a readable source for numerical claims. Retain designed graphics when they explain something clearly.

assessment.suggestion: Separate event photos and charts into carousels
assessment.reason: Use a field photograph, a sourced chart and a practical implication on separate pages. That is a readability proposal; the saved previews do not reveal carousel completion or prove a reach advantage.

assessment.suggestion: Set a narrative before each mission
assessment.reason: Agree on the audience, one question, the evidence to capture and the next conversation sought. A phrase such as “Grids for development” should organize the material, not replace the substantive claim.

assessment.decision: Give each channel a specific task
assessment.reason: LinkedIn develops the argument; Instagram makes the work visible; the UNDP page holds the evidence and offer; targeted internal communication connects it to relevant country and partner teams. People may enter through any channel.

assessment.suggestion: Use UNDP pages for search and AI discovery
assessment.reason: Build useful, indexable explanatory pages and inspect actual search and AI visibility. Do not claim that UNDP’s domain guarantees inclusion or that an AI citation means a prospective partner visited.

assessment.suggestion: Offer selective webinars on methods and tools
assessment.reason: Define who needs the method and what decision it supports before inviting anyone. A JET methodology session or digital-tool demonstration should end with an agreed application, responsible colleague and next step.

assessment.suggestion: Make resource mobilization the main goal
assessment.reason: Choose relevant donor and delivery-partner groups, demonstrate a capability and record qualified follow-ups. Track resulting concepts and funding separately; reactions are an early signal, not a measure of income.

Invite a specific contribution from someone who has relevant experience. A colleague-to-colleague exchange about the evidence is valuable; repeated requests to tag contacts for reach are not the proposed approach.

evaluation.title: Content response
evaluation.text: For each test, record the topic, purpose, format and publication date. Compare results after the same elapsed period. Use impressions or reach to calculate response rates where account analytics are available; the existing archive’s raw counters cannot supply those rates.

evaluation.title: Audience fit
evaluation.text: Record substantive exchanges with the types of organizations and professionals the campaign sought to reach. Distinguish technical questions, requests for evidence and peer referrals from congratulations. Review identifiable participants’ public professional roles rather than treating every comment as equivalent.

evaluation.title: Qualified follow-up
evaluation.text: Count requests for a briefing, methodology or tool; relevant meetings held; and agreed next steps. Attach a campaign reference and an owner. Note whether a person arrived through a post, the website, an internal introduction or several contacts.

evaluation.title: Programme and funding outcomes
evaluation.text: Record concept development, technical-assistance requests and donor discussions. Report committed funding only when confirmed through the normal organizational process. A campaign can contribute to an opportunity without being its sole cause.
